analysis: What changed vs the 8:00 AM brief: the broad selloff held rather than deepened — the S&P is still around -1.5% late morning and the Dow only -0.65% — but the chip complex got worse (SMH -6.5%, SOXL -24%, SanDisk -11.4%, Qualcomm -11.3%) while Amazon clawed back most of its loss, narrowing to -1.31% from an intraday low near $229.58. That divergence is the morning's real signal: dip-buying showed up in Amazon and in the non-chip megacaps (Alphabet -0.19%, Meta -0.22%, Tesla -0.73% late morning), while Intel (-28.35%, near its worst day since 1974) and Reddit (-28.5%, worst day since listing) are being priced on their own guides, not the market. Breadth is still poor — about 3 in 10 stocks rising, new lows (368) ahead of new highs (231) — but energy, staples and health care are holding up, and the VIX at 19.84 with TLT only +0.3% reads as equity selling, not a rates scare. Macro is not the driver: Q3 ECI came in at +0.8%, exactly as expected and cooler than Q2's +0.9%. Noise: the month-end concentration stat — 75% of S&P stocks are up for October yet the index is -0.5% for the month because the top 10 names are ~40% of it — explains why the tape looks worse than the typical stock. The next test is the close: SPY sits at 758.20, below Thursday's 766.6 low and its 21-day average, with the 30-week average near 749 underneath.

community_signals.takeaway: The WSB discussion analysis flags two things beyond the headlines: the irony in the Reddit trade (Google trained AI on Reddit content, then AI summaries cut its referrals) and the rotation into defense, while also tracking Amazon's V-shaped recovery and the chip rout in real time.

headlines.headline: Late morning: the selloff is holding, not cascading — SPY -1.47% at 758.20 (low 757.30, failed to reclaim 761 since the open), QQQ -2.97% at 694.17, Dow -0.65%; Yahoo snapshots at 8:20 AM PT had Nasdaq -2.32% at 25,578.17, S&P 500 -1.45% at 7,608.08, Dow -0.63% at 52,013.60.
headlines.why_it_matters: SPY stuck below Thursday's 766.6 low into late morning shows sellers still control the tape — but the Dow's small loss keeps this a tech-led decline, not a broad rout.

headlines.headline: Amazon staged a V-shaped recovery late morning to $240.56, down only 1.31%, rebounding nearly 5% from its intraday low of $229.58 — after Q3 revenue $201.9B vs ~$202.2B expected, EPS $1.89 vs ~$1.97, and trailing-12-month free cash flow of -$42.4B.
headlines.why_it_matters: A 5% intraday round-trip in Amazon shows dip-buying is alive in the name even while the cash-flow debate is unresolved — the morning low, not the premarket gap, is now the level to watch.

headlines.headline: Intel fell further to $65.98, down 28.35% (intraday low $64.13), near its worst session since 1974, on the Q4 guide ($15-16B revenue, ~$0.25 EPS vs ~$17.1B/$0.43 expected); Barron's adds Intel said it does not expect positive free cash flow in 2027, an 'investment year,' and a factory explosion in Israel caused a two-week shutdown costing roughly $600M in revenue over two quarters.
headlines.why_it_matters: The 2027 cash-flow warning plus a factory disruption turns a weak guide into a multi-quarter story — which is why Intel keeps dragging chips down with it instead of bouncing.

headlines.headline: Chip rout deepened late morning: SOX proxy SMH -6.5%, SOXL -24%, SanDisk -11.4%, Qualcomm -11.3%, AMD -9.8%, Micron -5.2%, Nvidia -3.6% at $205.97 near its intraday low; the SOX is down 13% since its October high and 21% from its June all-time high.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even Nvidia near its lows while the rest of the complex falls double-digits shows this is a sector de-rating, not a single-stock event — the AI-hardware trade is repricing as a group.

headlines.headline: Reddit fell to $92.77, down 28.5% near its intraday low and on track for its worst day since listing, after warning Q4 daily active uniques could fall by a low double-digit percentage and guiding Q4 revenue $1.00-1.03B vs ~$1.05B consensus; the company plans to require sign-ins for most content to deter AI scraping, while B. Riley kept Buy but cut its target to $190 from $270 and Citizens and KeyBanc downgraded.
headlines.why_it_matters: A sign-in wall is a direct response to the AI-search traffic loss — the debate is now whether Reddit can convert logged-out search visitors into registered users, not just whether Q4 guides low.

headlines.headline: Microsoft held up best among the AI spenders: down about 1% to ~$524.84, its fourth straight down session but only ~1% lower across that stretch, after fiscal Q1 revenue rose 19% to $92.3B with Azure up 48%; 27 firms raised price targets after earnings (Morgan Stanley to $650, BofA to $630), and Microsoft offered voluntary exits to 60,000 employees to cut costs for the AI buildout.
headlines.why_it_matters: Wall Street raising targets into a down tape is why Microsoft is the relative shelter in this selloff — its cash story, not just its cloud growth, is what investors are paying for.

headlines.headline: Non-chip megacaps nearly flat late morning: Alphabet $283.01 (-0.19%), Meta $623.11 (-0.22%), Tesla $400.41 (-0.73% after briefly reaching $404.12); Tesla remains up about 5% for the week, still the week's best Magnificent Seven performer, while Alphabet and Amazon are the week's worst after earnings.
headlines.why_it_matters: Megacaps ex-chips stabilizing near flat while semis fall double-digits shows the market is separating earnings stories from the AI-spending theme — the selloff is selective, not indiscriminate.

headlines.headline: Macro: Q3 Employment Cost Index rose 0.8%, exactly as expected and down from 0.9% in Q2; wages rose 0.7%, benefits 0.9%, and total compensation rose 3.4% year over year, while inflation-adjusted wages fell 0.6% over the year; the Fed held rates at 3.75%-4.00% on Wednesday.
headlines.why_it_matters: An in-line, cooling ECI keeps wage inflation from becoming a second story today — it leaves the Fed-speaker read later as the only macro event that could move the tape.

headlines.headline: Month-end concentration check (Morningstar): the S&P 500 is down 0.5% for October through Friday morning even though 75% of its stocks are up for the month, because the top 10 names are about 40% of the index; October losers among them: Alphabet -18.5%, Meta -14.7%, Micron -16.8%, Nvidia -8.7%, Amazon -6.9%; winners: Apple +4.2%, Microsoft +1.8%, Tesla +10.5%, Eli Lilly +23.5% (which also beat and raised guidance, up 4.4% Friday).
headlines.why_it_matters: The index-month looks worse than the typical stock's month — a reminder that this selloff is concentrated in the biggest AI names, which is also why the Dow is holding up far better than the Nasdaq.

headlines.headline: Apple reports fiscal Q4 after the close Monday Nov 2 — consensus around $113.3B revenue and $1.99 EPS, at the top of Apple's 9-11% growth guide, in new CEO John Ternus's first earnings call; the quarter includes only about nine days of iPhone 18 Pro sales, and Monness raised its target to $355 (Buy) while Bernstein reiterated Outperform at $370.
headlines.why_it_matters: With the quarter mostly pre-iPhone 18 Pro, the December-quarter guide matters more than the September print — Apple is the last megacap verdict on the AI-spending question.
